artifacts.summary: Full design research for a new generic typescript extension: file manifest with line budgets, context/project/typescript/ tree, both agents' stages/tools/model tier, hard_contracts recommendation, keyword_overrides set with an explicit collision check against web and 6 other manifests (none found), the typescript-rules.md paths glob, the verification hook's toolchain-detection and honest-degrade contract, and a line-level split of web's typescript-web.md.

next_steps: Run /orchestrate 620 to create the implementation plan from this research report

memory_candidates.content: When designing a new domain extension's keyword_overrides, the collision check needs two separate sources, not one: (1) read every OTHER loaded/source-store extension manifest's own keyword_overrides block directly (jq/python dump), and (2) read the core weak-signal fallback table in scripts/lib/task-type-detect.sh's DTD_WEAK_SIGNAL_TABLE, since a sibling extension with zero keyword_overrides (e.g. web) can still have a weak-signal row in the SAME core table that a naive 'does the sibling manifest declare keyword_overrides' check would miss entirely.

No extension in this repository's source store currently declares a verification-stage lifecycle hook (only nix and nvim use preflight/context_injection). The closest structural precedent, nix-preflight.sh, only ever warns-and-continues and never has to distinguish 'ran a check and it passed' from 'had nothing to check' -- a genuinely new design requirement (honest-degrade: SKIP with a stated reason, never a silent pass) has no adaptable precedent in-repo and must state its own three-state vocabulary (ran_pass/ran_fail/skipped_no_command) from scratch.
